subject.title: [Feature Request] Per-context configWrites permissions for all channel types

question: Should OpenClaw add context-scoped config-write authorization to the shared channel/plugin contract, and what context identity, inheritance, and deny-precedence rules should it use?
rationale: This changes a security boundary and public config/API semantics across channels, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent policy shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Shared Context Policy
options.body: Add a generic context identity and inheritance model first, then update bundled channels and docs against that shared contract.

options.title: Keep Channel/Account Only
options.body: Reject this feature for now and document separate accounts or operator procedures as the supported security boundary.

options.title: Patch One Channel First
options.body: Implement a channel-specific override for the highest-demand transport, accepting temporary semantic drift until a generic contract follows.

recommendation.title: Design Shared Context Policy
recommendation.body: Add a generic context identity and inheritance model first, then update bundled channels and docs against that shared contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shared policy and SDK helper history point most strongly to steipete for the cross-channel contract decision.
